text: OVERDOSAGE Symptoms Excessive or too rapid administration may produce alkalosis. Severe alkalosis may be accompanied by hyperirritability or tetany. (See ADVERSE REACTIONS ). Treatment Sodium bicarbonate should be discontinued and the symptoms of alkalosis controlled by rebreathing expired air from a paper bag or rebreathing mask or, if more severe, by parenteral injections of calcium gluconate. Severe alkalosis may be corrected by I.V. infusion of 2.14% ammonium chloride solution, except in patients with hepatic disease, in whom ammonia use is contraindicated. Sodium chloride (0.9%) I.V. or potassium chloride may be indicated if there is hypokalemia. Calcium gluconate is administered to control tetany.
